narration.text: Why one town waits 360–410 years for totality.
Somewhere on Earth, one happens every 18 months.
But the Moon's full shadow is only 100 to 160 kilometres wide.
So each eclipse touches just a thin strip of the planet.
Totality lasts minutes; the longest calculated reaches 7 minutes 29 seconds.
That's why eclipse chasers travel to the path.
So total eclipses are common for Earth, and rare for you.
